```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", dpi = 150)
```

`brainconn()` draws one image, so an animation is a series of images, one per time point, joined into a GIF. Here node colour and size show a value that changes over time. The [gifski](https://cran.r-project.org/package=gifski) package joins the images.

```{r}
library(brainconn)
atlas <- schaefer300_n7
```

## Spreading through the network

A network diffusion model (NDM) describes something, such as a disease process, spreading from a seed region along the connections of a network: the amount in each region at time `t` is `x(t) = exp(-L * t) %*% x0`, where `L` is the network's Laplacian matrix and `x0` the starting amounts. Adding it up over time gives the total that has reached each region, which only grows, so regions light up as the spread reaches them.

First a network. Here each region keeps its 10 strongest positive connections in the simulated `example_fc_schaefer300`; in practice you would use a structural connectome.

```{r}
A <- pmax(example_fc_schaefer300, 0)
diag(A) <- 0
strongest <- t(apply(A, 1, function(r) r >= sort(r, decreasing = TRUE)[10]))
A <- A * (strongest | t(strongest))
L <- diag(rowSums(A)) - A   # the Laplacian
```

Then the spread from a seed in the left temporal pole, at 30 time points:

```{r}
x0 <- as.numeric(atlas$ROI.Name == "Limbic_TempPole_1" & atlas$hemi == "LH")
e <- eigen(L, symmetric = TRUE)
total <- function(t) ifelse(e$values > 1e-9, (1 - exp(-e$values * t)) / e$values, t)
times <- seq(0, 20, length.out = 30)
x <- sapply(times, function(t) e$vectors %*% (total(t) * crossprod(e$vectors, x0)))
x <- pmin(pmax(x / max(x[x0 == 0, ]), 0), 1)   # 0 to 1 for colouring
```

Each time point is one image. Here is the 12th:

```{r, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5, out.width = "55%"}
colours <- colorRampPalette(c("grey85", "gold", "orange", "red", "darkred"))(100)
frame <- function(value, title) {
  brainconn(atlas = atlas, all.nodes = TRUE, view = "left", res = 600,
            node.size = 3 + 9 * value, node.color = colours[1 + round(value * 99)],
            hemi.labels = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::ggtitle(title)
}
frame(x[, 12], sprintf("t = %.0f", times[12]))
```

And `gifski::save_gif()` turns them into a GIF:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
gifski::save_gif({
  for (i in seq_along(times)) print(frame(x[, i], sprintf("t = %.0f", times[i])))
}, "spread.gif", width = 600, height = 500, delay = 0.15)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "60%"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/animation-spread.gif")
```

## A travelling wave

Any value per region and time point works the same way. Here a wave of activity sweeps from the back of the brain to the front. Because it is periodic, the GIF loops smoothly.

```{r}
y <- (atlas$y.mni - min(atlas$y.mni)) / diff(range(atlas$y.mni))   # 0 = back, 1 = front
phases <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 25)[-25]
wave <- sapply(phases, function(p) (1 + cos(2 * pi * (y - p))) / 2)
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
gifski::save_gif({
  for (i in seq_along(phases)) print(frame(wave[, i], ""))
}, "wave.gif", width = 600, height = 500, delay = 0.08)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "60%"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/animation-wave.gif")
```

Other ideas: activity time courses from fMRI or EEG, a seed's connectivity at different thresholds, or a slowly rotating camera with `view = c(azimuth, 20)` for azimuths from 0 to 360.
